text_blocks.snippet: A gallstones diet should focus on being healthy and balanced, with plenty of fiber and moderate fat intake. It's important to eat regular meals and avoid skipping them, as this can worsen symptoms.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on being healthy and balanced, with plenty of fiber and moderate fat intake

list.snippet: High-fiber foods: Fruits, vegetables, beans, pulses, oats, and whole grains are excellent sources of fiber.
Lean protein: Choose lean meats, fish (like sardines), and plant-based protein sources like beans, lentils, and tofu.
Healthy fats: Unsaturated fats from plant sources like olive oil, avocados, nuts, and seeds are preferable to saturated fats from animal products.
Low-fat dairy: Opt for low-fat or skimmed milk, yogurt, and cheese.
Fruits and vegetables: Aim for at least five portions per day.
Plenty of fluids: Drink at least 2 liters of water or herbal teas daily.

list.title: High-fat foods:
list.snippet: Reduce intake of foods high in saturated and trans fats, such as fatty meats, fried foods, pastries, and processed snacks.

list.title: Large meals:
list.snippet: Some individuals find that smaller, more frequent meals can help reduce symptoms.

list.title: Foods that trigger symptoms:
list.snippet: If you notice that certain foods cause pain or discomfort, consider avoiding them for a trial period.
Choose lower-fat options: When available, select reduced-fat versions of dairy products, spreads, and sauces.
Cook foods with healthier methods: Opt for grilling, poaching, steaming, or boiling instead of frying.
Read food labels carefully: Look for options that are low in fat and sugar.
Consider portion sizes: Larger meals can sometimes trigger symptoms, so smaller, more frequent meals may be helpful.
